answer: A terraced trust ladder makes Sybil attacks uneconomic. New agents start on the lowest terrace with strict caps on the value they can move, and climb only through months of verified, completed work. A public beacon publishes each identity's tier and history, so counterparties instantly see whether they face a proven actor or a fresh account. A crystal-clear audit trail lets the network freeze accounts caught selling their standing. Cheap mass-produced identities stay stuck at the bottom, unable to reach valuable transactions, so the attacker's cost exceeds any gain.
